question.leadin: A modern country named for this empire has its capital at Bamako.
question.text: Name this north African empire ruled by Sundiata Keita and Mansa Musa.
question.clue: Kanou built this empire's University at Sankore, and this empire was founded when Sundiata Keita defeated Soumaoro at the Battle of Kirina.

swap.text: Merchants from this empire and the later Songhai Empire partook in the trans-Saharan trade. This empire's ruler Mansa Musa disrupted the Egyptian economy by handing out gold during his trip to Mecca.
swap.clue: That founder defeated the Sosso monarch Sumanguru at the Battle of Kirina.

question.text: 1493 also featured Askia Muhammad usurping Sonni Baru to become leader of this empire. He would later enact many political and religious reforms within this empire, though it wouldn't reach the extent it did under Sonni Ali.
question.clue: Forces of this empire were lead by Ishaq II when it lost to Moroccan forces at Tondibi.

swap.leadin: Answer the following questions about Bartholomeu Dias.
swap.text: On his way back from a voyage, Dias discovered and rounded this cape on the southern tip of Africa. Dias gave this cape the name "Cape of Storms," though John II later gave it a more optimistic name.
swap.clue: This place is the southern extreme of a peninsula whose northern border is defined by Table Mountain.

question.leadin: There were many antebellum attempts to compromise between the North and the South.
question.text: This African country was founded from a colony for former slaves and free blacks as a way to remove them from the United States.
question.clue: Perhaps its most controversial leader declared his "national unification policy" and announced an "open door policy," constructing the largest mercantile fleet in the world.

swap.leadin: The Simba Rebellion was part of a 1960s crisis in this modern-day country.
swap.text: Identify this former Belgian colony whose first post-independence prime minister, Patrice Lumumba, was executed in its breakaway region of Katanga.
swap.answerHtml: Democratic Republic of the Congo [or DRC; or Congo-Kinshasa; do not accept “Republic of the Congo”; prompt on “Congo”]
swap.clue: A Luba chieftain led a split of one party in this country into the MNC-L and the MNC-K before leading the brief secessionist state South-Kasai, while Moise Tshombe led this country's secessionist Katanga province.

question.text: Rhodes was Prime Minister of the Cape Colony, a settlement in this modern-day country. In this modern-day country, Afrikaans-speaking Boers fought two wars against the British Empire.
question.clue: In that song, musicians pledged to not play at a casino resort in this country, "Sun City".

swap.text: The Himyarites fell after an invasion by this Ethiopian kingdom which adopted Christianity under its king Ezana. This kingdom was supposedly founded by the Queen of Sheba and was known for constructing many stelae.
swap.clue: This kingdom is the setting of a work about the transfer of th Ark of the Covenant to this place by the son of Makeda, the Kebra Negast.

question.leadin: Sculptors like Bernard Matemera and Joram Mariga were inspired by the shapes of objects found at this site.
question.text: Name this medieval city whose name is a corruption for the Shona words for "houses of stone." This city rose in power after the decline of the earlier Mapungubwe state.
question.clue: Mapungubwe preceded it, and Mutapa followed it, in control of the gold trade to Kilwa and the Islamic Indian Ocean network.

swap.text: This Ethiopian emperor built a railway from Djibouti to Addis Ababa and obtained European recognition of Ethiopian sovereignty following the Battle of Adowa.
swap.clue: As a child, this ruler reportedly wept when his father was taken prisoner by the government of Theodore II.

question.leadin: Winston Tubman criticized the awarding of the 2011 Nobel Peace Prize to this leader just prior to her re-election.
question.text: Name this leader who shared that prize with Leymah Gbowee, head of a women's peace movement in this leader's country. This leader first came to power after defeating George Weah in a 2005 election.
question.answerHtml: Ellen Johnson Sirleaf [accept Ellen Eugenia Johnson; accept either name]
question.clue: This African leader who, years after being exiled by Samuel Doe, led the Unity Party to victory in the 2005 Presidential Election against George Weah.

swap.leadin: This man's authenticite campaign resulted in cities such as Stanleyville and Elisabethville being renamed to Kisangani and Lubumbashi.
swap.text: Name this dictator who ruled Zaire until being overthrown in 1997. This dictator took power after overthrowing Patrice Lumumba and was notorious for embezzling massive amounts of money from the country during his reign.
swap.clue: This man sponsored a fight between Joe Frazier and Muhammad Ali and changed his name from Joseph to a Swahili phrase meaning "the invincible warrior who goes from conquest to conquest leaving fire in his wake".

question.text: This president of the Movement for the Survival of the Ogoni People campaigned against Royal Dutch Shell's destruction of Ogoni lands. He was hanged on the orders of Sani Abacha's government.
question.clue: This man wrote the memoir A Month and a Day recounting his detention by the government of Ibrahim Babangida.

swap.text: Busaidi rule in Zanzibar continued until 1964, when it was overthrown and annexed into neighboring Tanganyika under the direction of this leader, who later declared a policy of socialism under the Arusha Declaration.
swap.clue: A pan-Africanist, he provided homes to Mozambique's FRELIMO and South Africa's ANC.

question.text: According to most stories, Ndiadiane Ndiaye's father was a ruler of this dynasty from modern Morocco. This dynasty's rule ended with the fall of Marrakesh in 1147, and it may have conquered Ghana.
question.clue: Earlier, at the earlier battle of Sagrajas, its most successful leader, Yusuf ibn Tashfin, won a decisive victory over forces under Alfonso VI.

swap.leadin: A kingdom of these people was ruled by a line of queens known as Kabara, one of whom married an adventurer from Baghdad named Bayajidda.
swap.text: Name these people whose seven kingdoms were founded by Bayajidda's sons. These kingdoms included Gobir and Kano, the latter of which was ruled by the semi-mythical queen Amina.
swap.clue: A giant water-hoarding serpent called Sarki menaced this culture, and was slain by the exiled Abbasid prince Bayajidda ("buh-YAH-jid-duh"), who then founded its seven great cities, including Daura and Katsina.

question.leadin: This man's victory at the Battle of Dulmadobe in 1913 led to reprisals such as the 1920 bombing of Taalex.
question.text: Name this poet-warrior who fought British, Italian, and Ethiopian forces on behalf of his "dervish state" of Salihiyah Muslims.
question.answerHtml: the “Mad Mullah” [or Sayyid Maxamed Cabdulle Xasan; or Mohammed Abdullah Hassan]
question.clue: This man died unceremoniously of influenza in Ogaden after the Royal Air Force bombarded his capital at Taleh with impunity since his followers thought the planes were the chariots of Allah planning to take them up to heaven.

swap.leadin: One side in this conflict was led by Abd el Krim.
swap.text: Identify this conflict, which witnessed the Disaster of Annual, a major defeat for Manuel Fernandez Silvestre in 1921.
swap.clue: Francisco Franco served as a commander of the Tercio de Extranjeros during this war, in which Hugo Stoltzenberg supplied one side in this war with mustard gas, which broke the will of troops led by Abd el-Krim.

question.leadin: One king of this empire had several white Christian missionaries executed in 1885, including Bishop James Hannington, perhaps because they refused to have gay sex with him.
question.text: Name the empire whose last ruler was that man, Mwanga II, who reached a settlement with the British in 1892.
question.clue: This kingdom's Kasubi Tombs inter the bisexual king Mwanga II, who executed Christian martyrs and allied with Lord Lugard's protectorate against its former hegemon ("HEDGE-uh-mon") Bunyoro.

swap.leadin: This location became the headquarters for the MLC after its 1998 capture by Jean-Pierre Bemba.
swap.text: Name this town on the Ubangi River, whose airport was built to accommodate the supersonic Concorde for quick shopping trips to Paris. This "Versailles of the Jungle" was once home to a nuclear bunker and a complex of Chinese pagodas, though it now lies in ruin.
